phase: P6.2 tensor-TP same-device spike - attribution witness and verdict
hardware: 1x AMD Instinct MI50 32 GB (HIP device 0), ROCm 7.2.0; host 125 GiB; engine ds41_generate build-906

w1_witness.note: pre-fix loader (4 dead indexer slices); runner guard formula bug refused the first attempt

w2_attribution.verdict_input: FA split costs nothing: tp_nofa (+40.5%) equals tp (+39.0%) within noise

w3_bonly_cold_control.note: control here is CONTAMINATED: the intervening vLLM restart evicted the GGUF page cache and the first boot re-read it from NVMe; this session is the witness that first-boot cache warmth alone can move a control run 2.4x. Numbers not used in the verdict; it motivated the throwaway warmup boot now in the runner.

w4_definitive.setup: throwaway warmup boot, then control, tp, tp_nofa, tp_b, same session, same binary, slots 1500 all arms, 512-token prompt chunk 64, n=128
w4_definitive.tokens: all arms 128/128 identical to control (three sessions, every arm, zero knife-edge flips)
w4_definitive.decode_instability: the tp (FA-split) arm decoded at 5.90 tok/s here and 13.81 in w2, same binary, same args, 2nd boot in both sessions; MoE tier counters are identical between the runs (97.7% VRAM hits, same file/cpu ms), so the extra ~96 ms/token sits in the dense/attention path itself. Unexplained; treated as a risk of the FA-split shape, not of the reduce node (tp_nofa/tp_b decodes never moved).

attribution.fa_split: w2: tp - tp_nofa ~ 0 - the two half-head flash-attn launches cost nothing on this device
attribution.gemm_reduce_path: w4 tp_b: full FA + full output_a, ONLY attn_output_b halved into two mul_mats over row-views plus the single f32 add, still +41.1% at 10/40 layers - the half-k mul_mat path (or the views feeding it) is where prefill TP dies
attribution.noise_hygiene: control absolute rate is session-dependent (11.0-26.9 tok/s): first-boot page-cache state after another tenant (vLLM) ran between sessions; warmup boot added to the runner. Within sessions arms ran 2nd/3rd/4th behind control; a monotone late-boot drag would FAVOR none of the arms' verdicts, and tp_b ran LAST yet still lost 41% to the first arm.

kill_gate.rule: same-device 2-shard overhead > 10% at n=64 means GEMM halving cannot win and cross-card prefill TP is NO-GO (P6.2 rule, docs/gfx906/P6-TENSOR-SPLIT.md)
kill_gate.measured: tp +26..+45%, tp_nofa +40..+45%, tp_b +41% at 10 of 40 layers, three sessions
kill_gate.verdict: PREFILL TENSOR-TP: NO-GO. A cross-card split would put ONE half-k mul_mat per card - exactly the op measured pathological even in the minimal tp_b arm - plus a bounce allreduce on top. Halving the GEMM does not halve its time on this ggml/HIP path; the reduction and the split itself cost more than the GEMM halves save.

what_still_holds: The seam ALGEBRA is certified: reduce node composes with the hc machine and per-column carry, 128/128 identical greedy tokens in every arm in every session across 8 chunked-prefill passes and 128 decodes; the graph cache, sliced-weight loader and per-shard flash-attn all build and replay correctly. If a future kernel path makes half-k mul_mats pay their byte-bound share, w4 is the measurement to re-take; the spike code (opt-in, default byte-identical) and the three-arm runner stay on the branch for that day.
not_tested: cross-card placement (each card one half-GEMM): the same-device spike measures both halves on one device per the plan's gate design; m-axis (output-column) splits were considered and rejected on paper because every hc_post/rms_norm mixes across D; decode weight-read-split benefit needs cross-card wiring and is NOT answered by any same-device number - the tp decode flakiness (5.90 vs 13.81) is itself a warning there.
